title: Genesis 1 — When the Elohim began to shape

paragraphs.text: בְּרֵאשִׁ֖ית בָּרָ֣א אֱלֹהִ֑ים אֵ֥ת הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וְאֵ֥ת הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: When the Elohim began to shape the skies and the land—
i18n.he: בְּרֵאשִׁ֖ית בָּרָ֣א אֱלֹהִ֑ים אֵ֥ת הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וְאֵ֥ת הָאָֽרֶץ׃
i18n.de: Als die Elohim begannen, die Himmel und das Land zu formen—
i18n.es: Cuando los Elohim comenzaron a formar los cielos y la tierra—
i18n.fr: Quand les Elohim commencèrent à façonner les cieux et la terre—
i18n.ja: エロヒムが天と地を形づくり始めたとき—
i18n.ko: 엘로힘이 하늘과 땅을 빚기 시작했을 때—
i18n.ru: Когда Элохим начали придавать форму небесам и земле—
i18n.zh: 当厄罗音开始塑造诸天与大地之时——
i18n.zh-Hant: 當厄羅音開始塑造諸天與大地之時—

notes.official:
**Three load-bearing choices in one verse.**

*Bereshit* is grammatically a construct form **without** the definite article — בְּרֵאשִׁית means "in beginning-of", not "in **the** beginning" (which would require בָּרֵאשִׁית). The verse is a temporal clause introducing v2 and v3, not a freestanding declaration. The Rashi-favoured reading, also adopted by NJPS, NRSV, and most modern scholarly translations, treats the construct as it stands: *When the Elohim began to shape …* The traditional "In the beginning" carries a *creatio-ex-nihilo* doctrinal commitment the Hebrew doesn't grammatically support. Restoring the construct lets the text describe a project beginning, not the absolute origin of all matter.

*Bara* is one of three creation verbs Genesis 1 deploys deliberately (with *asah* "make" and *yatsar* "form"). Standard translations flatten all three into "create/make", losing the pattern. *Bara* in the Qal denotes shaping or fashioning; the Piel of the same root means "cut out, fashion". Rendering as **shape** preserves the verb's distinctness without inserting a metaphysical claim either way. The verb returns in v21 (sea-creatures) and v27 (humankind) — three categorical moments out of dozens of creative acts in the chapter.

*Elohim* is grammatically masculine plural (-im ending). The singular "God" is a theological smoothing inherited from the LXX's choice to render with singular Θεός. The plural form is preserved untranslated. Plural verbs and pronouns governing the Elohim are flagged where they appear (see v26).

*Shamayim* is grammatically dual (the -ayim ending). Hebrew has no singular form for sky/heaven. **Skies** preserves the dual. *Eretz* covers a spectrum from "patch of ground" to "inhabited territory". The capital-E "Earth" (the planet) is a 17th-century English meaning the Hebrew doesn't carry. **Land** is closer to the register.

*The modern debate.* Reading *bara* as reorganization rather than creation-from-nothing is not only Rashi's move; it has a peer-reviewed contemporary defender. Ellen van Wolde argued in the *Journal for the Study of the Old Testament* (2009) that *bara* in Genesis 1 means "to spatially separate" — the deity dividing an already-existing cosmos into its regions — a proposal contested among Hebraists but argued as scholarship, not doctrine. Whether or not the specific "separate" gloss holds, it places the reading of the verb without the *creatio-ex-nihilo* commitment inside live academic debate rather than outside it.

paragraphs.text: וְהָאָ֗רֶץ הָיְתָ֥ה תֹ֙הוּ֙ וָבֹ֔הוּ וְחֹ֖שֶׁךְ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י תְה֑וֹם וְר֣וּחַ אֱלֹהִ֔ים מְרַחֶ֖פֶת עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַמָּֽיִם׃

i18n.he: וְהָאָ֗רֶץ הָיְתָ֥ה תֹ֙הוּ֙ וָבֹ֔הוּ וְחֹ֖שֶׁךְ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י תְה֑וֹם וְר֣וּחַ אֱלֹהִ֔ים מְרַחֶ֖פֶת עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַמָּֽיִם׃
i18n.de: —wobei das Land Wüstenei und Leere war, mit Finsternis über dem Angesicht der Tiefe, und der Hauch der Elohim über dem Angesicht der Wasser schwebte—
i18n.es: —siendo la tierra páramo y vacío, con tinieblas sobre la faz del abismo, y el aliento de los Elohim cerniéndose sobre la faz de las aguas—
i18n.fr: —la terre étant désolation et vide, avec les ténèbres sur la face de l'abîme, et le souffle des Elohim planant sur la face des eaux—
i18n.ja: —地は荒涼として虚しく、闇が深淵の面を覆い、エロヒムの息が水の面の上を漂っていた—
i18n.ko: —땅은 황무함과 공허함이었고, 어둠이 깊음의 표면을 덮고 있었으며, 엘로힘의 숨결이 물의 표면 위를 맴돌고 있었다—
i18n.ru: —земля была пустошью и пустотой, и тьма над поверхностью бездны, и дыхание Элохим парило над поверхностью вод—
i18n.zh: ——大地一片荒芜空虚，黑暗笼罩深渊之面，厄罗音的气息盘旋于众水之面——
i18n.zh-Hant: —大地一片荒蕪與空虛，黑暗籠罩著深淵的表面，厄羅音的氣息盤旋在水面之上—

notes.official:
**The single most contested choice in this chapter.**

*Ruach Elohim* — רוּחַ has three lexical fields: **breath**, **wind**, **spirit**. Hebrew does not disambiguate; context is the only guide. KJV/ASV's "Spirit of God" is a Trinitarian-tradition reading retrojected onto Gen 1:2; the Hebrew supports "wind" (NJPS: "a wind from God"), "breath", or "spirit" equally. The verb that follows — *merachefet* — specifically denotes **hovering/fluttering** (cf. Deut 32:11, an eagle hovering over its young). Wind hovers; breath hovers; *Spirit* doesn't, in any natural register. The WoH choice is **breath of the Elohim hovering**, preserving the verb's bird-image and the verse's physical/atmospheric register without importing a Trinitarian doctrinal claim.

*Tohu vavohu* — KJV "without form and void" reads philosophical (Aristotelian matter without form); the Hebrew is concrete. The pair appears together in Jer 4:23 describing a post-disaster depopulated landscape, and in Isa 34:11 (similar). **Wasteland and emptiness** preserves the alliterative pair (the -ohu / -ohu echo) and the concrete imagery.

*Tehom* is etymologically and conceptually cognate with Akkadian *tiāmtu* — the same root behind **Tiamat** of the *Enuma Elish*, where the goddess is the primordial salt-sea. Genesis has demythologized the term but preserved the word. The link is recorded in the glossary; the translation itself stays measured ("the deep").

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֖ים יְהִ֣י א֑וֹר וַֽיְהִי־אֽוֹר׃

i18n.en: The Elohim said, "Let there be light"; and there was light.
i18n.he: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֖ים יְהִ֣י א֑וֹר וַֽיְהִי־אֽוֹר׃
i18n.de: sagten die Elohim: "Es werde Licht"; und es wurde Licht.
i18n.es: los Elohim dijeron: «Haya luz»; y hubo luz.
i18n.fr: les Elohim dirent : « Que la lumière soit » ; et la lumière fut.
i18n.ja: エロヒムは言った、「光あれ」。すると光があった。
i18n.ko: 엘로힘이 말하였다, "빛이 있으라"; 그러자 빛이 있었다.
i18n.ru: Элохим сказали: «Да будет свет»; и стал свет.
i18n.zh: 厄罗音说：「要有光」；于是有了光。
i18n.zh-Hant: 厄羅音說：「要有光」；於是就有了光。

notes.official: Under the construct reading begun in v1, v3 is the **main clause** of the v1–v3 temporal structure: *When the Elohim began to shape ... the land being wasteland and emptiness ... the Elohim said, "Let there be light"*. The verse-initial "And" of older English translations is dropped — this is the first clause, not a continuation.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֧רְא אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת־הָא֖וֹר כִּי־ט֑וֹב וַיַּבְדֵּ֣ל אֱלֹהִ֔ים בֵּ֥ין הָא֖וֹר וּבֵ֥ין הַחֹֽשֶׁךְ׃

i18n.en: And the Elohim saw that the light was good; and the Elohim separated between the light and the darkness.
i18n.he: וַיַּ֧רְא אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת־הָא֖וֹר כִּי־ט֑וֹב וַיַּבְדֵּ֣ל אֱלֹהִ֔ים בֵּ֥ין הָא֖וֹר וּבֵ֥ין הַחֹֽשֶׁךְ׃
i18n.de: Und die Elohim sahen, dass das Licht gut war; und die Elohim schieden zwischen dem Licht und der Finsternis.
i18n.es: Y los Elohim vieron que la luz era buena; y los Elohim separaron entre la luz y las tinieblas.
i18n.fr: Et les Elohim virent que la lumière était bonne ; et les Elohim séparèrent la lumière des ténèbres.
i18n.ja: エロヒムはその光を見て、良しとした。そしてエロヒムは光と闇とを分けた。
i18n.ko: 엘로힘이 그 빛을 보니 좋았다; 엘로힘은 빛과 어둠 사이를 나누었다.
i18n.ru: И увидели Элохим, что свет хорош; и отделили Элохим свет от тьмы.
i18n.zh: 厄罗音看见光是好的；厄罗音便将光与暗分开。
i18n.zh-Hant: 厄羅音看見光是好的；厄羅音便將光與暗分開。

notes.official:
**Two structural firsts.** *Vayavdel* — from *badal*, **to separate, divide** — is the organizing verb of the opening triad. Days one through three proceed by division: light from darkness (here), the waters above from the waters below (v6–7), and the sea from the dry land (v9). The chapter's method is the separation of an existing continuum into ordered regions, not production from nothing — the same emphasis carried by the construct reading of v1 and by *bara* rendered *shape* rather than *create-from-nothing*.

*Ki tov* — **that it was good** — is the first of the sevenfold approval refrain (vv. 4, 10, 12, 18, 21, 25, and *tov me'od*, "very good", at v31). *Tov* here reads closer to **fit, sound, well-made** than to moral virtue: the maker inspects the work and finds it answers its purpose, the way a craftsman judges a finished piece. The refrain is a quality-control cadence, and its conspicuous absence on day two (see v8) is therefore a feature the text wants noticed.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֱלֹהִ֤ים ׀ לָאוֹר֙ י֔וֹם וְלַחֹ֖שֶׁךְ קָ֣רָא לָ֑יְלָה וַֽיְהִי־עֶ֥רֶב וַֽיְהִי־בֹ֖קֶר י֥וֹם אֶחָֽד׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And the Elohim called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And there was evening and there was morning, day one.
i18n.he: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֱלֹהִ֤ים ׀ לָאוֹר֙ י֔וֹם וְלַחֹ֖שֶׁךְ קָ֣רָא לָ֑יְלָה וַֽיְהִי־עֶ֥רֶב וַֽיְהִי־בֹ֖קֶר י֥וֹם אֶחָֽד׃ (פ)
i18n.de: Und die Elohim nannten das Licht Tag, und die Finsternis nannten sie Nacht. Und es wurde Abend und es wurde Morgen: Tag eins.
i18n.es: Y los Elohim llamaron a la luz Día, y a las tinieblas las llamaron Noche. Y hubo tarde y hubo mañana: día uno.
i18n.fr: Et les Elohim appelèrent la lumière Jour, et les ténèbres ils appelèrent Nuit. Il y eut un soir et il y eut un matin : premier jour.
i18n.ja: エロヒムは光を昼と呼び、闇を夜と呼んだ。夕となり朝となった。第一の日。
i18n.ko: 엘로힘은 빛을 낮이라 부르고, 어둠을 밤이라 불렀다. 저녁이 되고 아침이 되었다. 첫째 날.
i18n.ru: И назвали Элохим свет Днём, а тьму назвали Ночью. И был вечер, и было утро: день один.
i18n.zh: 厄罗音称光为昼，称暗为夜。有晚上，有早晨，第一日。
i18n.zh-Hant: 厄羅音稱光為晝，稱暗為夜。有晚上，有早晨，第一日。

notes.official: *Yom echad* — **day one**, cardinal *echad*, not the ordinal *rishon*. Hebrew uses the cardinal uniquely for day one, then switches to ordinals (*sheni, shlishi, …*) for days 2–6. Most English translations smooth to "first day" / "a second day" which loses the deliberate signaling. The numbered-day pattern in Hebrew is bookended: cardinal *echad* opens, definite *ha-shishi* ("the sixth day") closes (v31).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֔ים יְהִ֥י רָקִ֖יעַ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַמָּ֑יִם וִיהִ֣י מַבְדִּ֔יל בֵּ֥ין מַ֖יִם לָמָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And the Elohim said, "Let there be a dome in the midst of the waters, and let it separate between waters and waters."
i18n.he: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֔ים יְהִ֥י רָקִ֖יעַ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַמָּ֑יִם וִיהִ֣י מַבְדִּ֔יל בֵּ֥ין מַ֖יִם לָמָֽיִם׃
i18n.de: Und die Elohim sagten: "Es werde eine Wölbung inmitten der Wasser, und sie scheide zwischen Wassern und Wassern."
i18n.es: Y los Elohim dijeron: «Haya una bóveda en medio de las aguas, y separe entre aguas y aguas».
i18n.fr: Et les Elohim dirent : « Qu'il y ait une voûte au milieu des eaux, et qu'elle sépare les eaux d'avec les eaux. »
i18n.ja: エロヒムは言った、「水の中にドームあれ、そして水と水とを分けよ」。
i18n.ko: 엘로힘이 말하였다, "물 가운데에 궁창이 있어, 물과 물 사이를 나누도록 하라."
i18n.ru: И сказали Элохим: «Да будет свод посреди вод, и да отделяет он воды от вод».
i18n.zh: 厄罗音说：「在众水之中要有穹苍，将水与水分开。」
i18n.zh-Hant: 厄羅音說：「要在眾水之中有穹蒼，將水與水分開。」

notes.official: *Raqia* derives from the verb רקע — **to hammer out** (a metal sheet). The ANE cosmology is a solid vault hammered out across the sky to hold back the upper waters (cf. v6–7, where the *raqia* is explicitly placed *between* waters and waters). The LXX renders στερέωμα ("solid/firm thing"), whence Vulgate *firmamentum*, whence English **firmament**. Modern translations soften further to "expanse" (ESV, NIV), which papers over the solid-dome cosmology. The WoH choice is **dome** — accurate to the Hebrew picture, honest about the cosmology, and lets the reader make their own peace with the picture.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ אֱלֹהִים֮ אֶת־הָרָקִיעַ֒ וַיַּבְדֵּ֗ל בֵּ֤ין הַמַּ֙יִם֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ מִתַּ֣חַת לָרָקִ֔יעַ וּבֵ֣ין הַמַּ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֖ר מֵעַ֣ל לָרָקִ֑יעַ וַֽיְהִי־כֵֽן׃

i18n.en: And the Elohim made the dome, and separated between the waters which were under the dome and the waters which were above the dome. And it was so.
i18n.he: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ אֱלֹהִים֮ אֶת־הָרָקִיעַ֒ וַיַּבְדֵּ֗ל בֵּ֤ין הַמַּ֙יִם֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ מִתַּ֣חַת לָרָקִ֔יעַ וּבֵ֣ין הַמַּ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֖ר מֵעַ֣ל לָרָקִ֑יעַ וַֽיְהִי־כֵֽן׃
i18n.de: Und die Elohim machten die Wölbung und schieden zwischen den Wassern, die unter der Wölbung waren, und den Wassern, die über der Wölbung waren. Und so geschah es.
i18n.es: Y los Elohim hicieron la bóveda, y separaron entre las aguas que estaban debajo de la bóveda y las aguas que estaban sobre la bóveda. Y así fue.
i18n.fr: Et les Elohim firent la voûte, et séparèrent les eaux qui étaient sous la voûte des eaux qui étaient au-dessus de la voûte. Et il en fut ainsi.
i18n.ja: エロヒムはドームを造り、ドームの下の水とドームの上の水とを分けた。そのとおりになった。
i18n.ko: 엘로힘은 궁창을 만들어, 궁창 아래의 물과 궁창 위의 물 사이를 나누었다. 그렇게 되었다.
i18n.ru: И сделали Элохим свод, и отделили воды, которые под сводом, от вод, которые над сводом. И стало так.
i18n.zh: 厄罗音造出穹苍，将穹苍之下的水与穹苍之上的水分开。事就这样成了。
i18n.zh-Hant: 厄羅音造了穹蒼，將穹蒼以下的水與穹蒼以上的水分開。事就這樣成了。

notes.official: **Verb pattern point.** The dome is *made* (*asah*), not *shaped* (*bara*). The chapter alternates the verbs deliberately: *bara* is reserved for v1 (skies and land), v21 (the unprecedented sea-creatures), and v27 (humankind). Everything else — including the dome here — is *asah*. Most English translations interchange the two verbs freely; preserving them apart surfaces the deliberate categorical work the chapter is doing.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרָ֧א אֱלֹהִ֛ים לָֽרָקִ֖יעַ שָׁמָ֑יִם וַֽיְהִי־עֶ֥רֶב וַֽיְהִי־בֹ֖קֶר י֥וֹם שֵׁנִֽי׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And the Elohim called the dome Skies. And there was evening and there was morning, day two.
i18n.he: וַיִּקְרָ֧א אֱלֹהִ֛ים לָֽרָקִ֖יעַ שָׁמָ֑יִם וַֽיְהִי־עֶ֥רֶב וַֽיְהִי־בֹ֖קֶר י֥וֹם שֵׁנִֽי׃ (פ)
i18n.de: Und die Elohim nannten die Wölbung Himmel. Und es wurde Abend und es wurde Morgen: Tag zwei.
i18n.es: Y los Elohim llamaron a la bóveda Cielos. Y hubo tarde y hubo mañana: día segundo.
i18n.fr: Et les Elohim appelèrent la voûte Cieux. Il y eut un soir et il y eut un matin : deuxième jour.
i18n.ja: エロヒムはそのドームを天と呼んだ。夕となり朝となった。第二の日。
i18n.ko: 엘로힘은 궁창을 하늘이라 불렀다. 저녁이 되고 아침이 되었다. 둘째 날.
i18n.ru: И назвали Элохим свод Небесами. И был вечер, и было утро: день второй.
i18n.zh: 厄罗音称穹苍为诸天。有晚上，有早晨，第二日。
i18n.zh-Hant: 厄羅音稱穹蒼為諸天。有晚上，有早晨，第二日。

notes.official: **Note the absence of "the Elohim saw that it was good" on day 2.** This is a textual feature, not an omission, and has drawn rabbinic and modern scholarly comment for centuries. The standard explanations: (1) the project of separating the waters is not complete until day 3, when the dry land appears, so the "good" lands then (v10 closes day 2 *and* day 3's first work with a single "good"); (2) day 2's work is structural plumbing, not a final result. The omission is deliberate and intelligible. The translation preserves the absence without comment in the verse; the lens surfaces it here.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים יִקָּו֨וּ הַמַּ֜יִם מִתַּ֤חַת הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ אֶל־מָק֣וֹם אֶחָ֔ד וְתֵרָאֶ֖ה הַיַּבָּשָׁ֑ה וַֽיְהִי־כֵֽן׃

i18n.en: And the Elohim said, "Let the waters under the skies be gathered to one place, and let the dry ground appear." And it was so.
i18n.he: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים יִקָּו֨וּ הַמַּ֜יִם מִתַּ֤חַת הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ אֶל־מָק֣וֹם אֶחָ֔ד וְתֵרָאֶ֖ה הַיַּבָּשָׁ֑ה וַֽיְהִי־כֵֽן׃
i18n.de: Und die Elohim sagten: "Die Wasser unter den Himmeln sollen sich an einem Ort sammeln, und das trockene Land erscheine." Und so geschah es.

notes.official:
**The dry land is revealed, not made.** The ground does not come into being here; it *appears* (*teraeh*, niphal of *ra'ah*, "be seen") once the waters are **gathered** (*yikkavu*, niphal of *qavah*) to one place. The third day organizes what is already present, by drainage and collection — again separation rather than fabrication (cf. v1, v4). *Yabbashah* is specifically the **dry land**, the exposed ground, distinct from the named "Land" (*eretz*) of v10 and from the arable *adamah* of Gen 2.

The motif has a broad ancient Near Eastern background: cosmogonies from Mesopotamia and Egypt commonly begin with a watery expanse out of which a first dry mound emerges. Genesis keeps the opening image — a world under water, land emerging — while stripping away the combat and the theogony that surround it elsewhere (contrast *Enuma Elish*, where the sky is fashioned from the carcass of the slain sea-goddess Tiamat). Here the waters are simply commanded into place. The demythologizing is deliberate, and it is sharpened again at v16 and v21.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֱלֹהִ֤ים ׀ לַיַּבָּשָׁה֙ אֶ֔רֶץ וּלְמִקְוֵ֥ה הַמַּ֖יִם קָרָ֣א יַמִּ֑ים וַיַּ֥רְא אֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי־טֽוֹב׃

notes.official:
Capitalized **Land** here is a proper name (the Elohim is naming the dry ground), parallel to **Seas**. This is a naming moment within the chapter, distinct from the default-register *eretz* = "land" elsewhere.

The naming also quietly demilitarizes the sea. In the surrounding Canaanite world *yam* is a divine name — Yammu, the sea-god who contends with Baal — and the primeval waters are a hostile power to be subdued. Here the Elohim simply *names* the gathered waters **Seas** and pronounces them **good** (*ki tov*): the sea is a labelled, approved region of the ordered world, not an adversary. The same demythologizing hand will handle the *taninim*, the "great dragons", at v21.

notes.official:
**The land is made a co-maker, and the categories are fixed from the start.** The Elohim does not plant directly; the command *tadshe ha-aretz* — **let the land put forth** — makes the ground an agent that brings the vegetation out of itself. The same delegation recurs on day six, when the land is told to *bring forth* the living creatures (v24).

*Lemino* — **according to its kind** — enters here and becomes the signature refrain of the created biosphere (vv. 11, 12, 21, 24, 25). Coupled with *mazria zera*, **seed-bearing**, and fruit "in which is its seed", the verse describes life built to reproduce true to type: bounded kinds, each propagating within its own category.

For the Wheel of Heaven reading this is a load-bearing detail — the living world is presented as organized into seeded, self-perpetuating kinds, category-stable from the outset rather than shading continuously one into another. The translation makes no claim about the biology of speciation; it preserves the Hebrew's insistence on the boundedness. *(That the fixed-kinds motif marks a designed feature rather than a descriptive folk-taxonomy is a reading the WoH lens brings to the text; the Hebrew states the boundedness, not its cause.)*

notes.official:
*Meorot* — **luminaries**, not "lights". The Hebrew is a more technical word than *or* (light): it denotes **light-source objects**. The plural form returns through v14–v16 as the cosmos-organizing category that the chapter is positioning here.

*Moadim* — **appointed times**, not "seasons". The Hebrew has a technical calendrical sense — fixed times, festival appointments, predetermined astronomical occasions. The KJV/ASV "seasons" reads natural-cycles (spring/summer/autumn/winter); the Hebrew is structural-calendrical. The luminaries are positioned here as functional time-keepers, not as deities.

i18n.ru: И сделали Элохим два великих светила: светило большее—для управления днём, и светило меньшее—для управления ночью; и звёзды.
i18n.zh: 厄罗音造了两个大光体：较大的光体管理白昼，较小的光体管理黑夜；又造了众星。

notes.official:
**The most polemically charged verse in the chapter.** Hebrew has perfectly good words for **sun** (*shemesh*) and **moon** (*yareach*) and they are not used. Both terms were divinized in surrounding ANE traditions — *Shamash* (the sun god of Babylon, Sippar, Larsa), *Sin* (the Sumero-Akkadian moon god of Ur, Harran). Genesis 1 demythologizes them by naming them only by function: **the greater luminary** to govern day, **the lesser luminary** to govern night. The stars get one terminal half-line, almost as an afterthought ("and the stars"). The deliberate refusal of personal names is the polemic. Preserving "luminary" rather than smoothing back to "sun/moon" is non-optional under the WoH lens.

*Memshelet* — **governance**, a relatively technical political term ("dominion over a territory", "jurisdiction"), not just "rule". The luminaries are granted functional jurisdiction over day and night — the cosmos is being organized into administrative compartments assigned to functional bodies.

notes.official: *Nefesh chayah* — **living being**, not "living creature" or "living soul". *Nefesh* is famously hard: its lexical core is **breath / throat / self / life**, not a Platonic-detachable soul. The KJV "soul" (in Gen 2:7 for *ha-adam*) is the retrojection to avoid; modern Hebrew Bible studies consensus is firmly "being" or "creature". The translation uses **living being** consistently for *nefesh chayah*.

notes.official:
**The verb returns. And the polemic now shows.**

The dragons are *shaped* (*bara*), not *made* (*asah*). Why bara here, in the middle of a chapter that has been using asah for almost everything? Because *tanninim* (great dragons) is the Hebrew Bible's standard word for the serpent-dragon-monster class: rival figures elsewhere (Job 7:12 — "Am I a sea, or a *tannin*?"; Isaiah 27:1 — "the *tannin* that is in the sea" paired with Leviathan; Psalm 74:13 — "you broke the heads of the *tanninim* in the waters"; Ezekiel 29:3 — Pharaoh as the "great *tannin*"). The deliberate use of *bara* here is a **demythologizing** move — the same dragon-class beings other ANE traditions deify (Akkadian Tiamat, Ugaritic Lotan, Egyptian Apep) are something Elohim *shaped*, not fought.

*Tehom* in v2 — "the deep" — is etymologically cognate with Tiamat. The two halves of the polemic bracket the chapter: the primaeval-sea vocabulary of Genesis 1 is the cosmic-rival vocabulary of the Chaoskampf myths, and Genesis quietly reassigns every figure as a creature of the Elohim's project rather than as a rival to it.

*Taninim* — **great dragons** (revised from "great sea-creatures" in glossary v2.0.0). The Hebrew word itself contains no aquatic morpheme; the sea-association in this verse is positional (v20–22 frame), not lexical. KJV renders the same word "dragon(s)" almost everywhere else in the corpus (Deut 32:33, Ps 91:13, Isa 13:22, Isa 27:1, Jer 9:11, Ezek 29:3, Mal 1:3); only Gen 1:21 gets the euphemistic "whales". Modern translations soften to "sea-monsters" or "great sea-creatures" but the lexical case for dragon is the same here as in the prophets. The earlier "sea-creatures" rendering preserved the size+sea features at the cost of the dragon register — and therefore at the cost of the polemic the verse exists to perform. "Great dragons" lets the reader see the dragon-class creatures named, and see Elohim shaping them rather than fighting them.

A reader curious about whether the dragon-class folk memory across cultures (Mesopotamian, Egyptian, Greek, Chinese, European) might preserve impressions of actual creatures — whether of an earlier paleontological era, or, in the Wheel of Heaven reading, of stages in the Elohim's biological project — is invited to think about it. The translation does not encode the inference; it preserves what the Hebrew says.

i18n.ja: エロヒムはそれらを祝福して言った、「産めよ、増えよ、海の水を満たせ。また鳥は地に増えよ」。
i18n.ko: 엘로힘은 그것들에게 복을 주며 말하였다, "생육하고 번성하여 바다의 물을 채우라; 새들도 땅에서 번성하라."

i18n.zh-Hant: 厄羅音祝福牠們說：「要繁衍增多，充滿海洋中的水；鳥也要在大地上增多。」

notes.official:
**The first blessing, and the formula that will structure the book.** *Vayevarekh* — from *barakh*, **to bless** — appears here for the first time, spoken over the sea-swarm and the birds. In Genesis a blessing is not a sentiment but a conferred power, and its content is stated outright: *peru urevu* — **be fruitful and multiply**.

The formula binds the primeval history together. It is given to the animals here, to humankind at v28, and renewed to Noah and his sons after the flood (Gen 9:1, 7); the patriarchal promises are its narrowed, covenantal continuation. Its first recipients are non-human, which frames the human blessing of v28 as an intensification of a gift already granted to the living world — fertility, the capacity to fill a domain — rather than a category reserved for humankind alone.

i18n.ja: エロヒムは言った、「地は生き物をその種類にしたがって生じさせよ。家畜、這うもの、地の獣をその種類にしたがって生じさせよ」。そのとおりになった。
i18n.ko: 엘로힘이 말하였다, "땅은 그 종류대로 살아있는 생물을 내라: 가축과, 기는 것과, 그 종류대로 땅의 짐승을 내라." 그렇게 되었다.
i18n.ru: И сказали Элохим: «Да произведёт земля живых существ по их роду: скот, и пресмыкающихся, и зверей земных по их роду». И стало так.
i18n.zh: 厄罗音说：「大地要按类生出活物：牲畜、爬行之物，以及按其类的大地走兽。」事就这样成了。
i18n.zh-Hant: 厄羅音說：「大地要按其種類產出活物：牲畜、爬行類，以及按其種類的大地走獸。」事就這樣成了。

notes.official:
**Day six opens by echoing day three: the land is again told to produce.** *Totse ha-aretz* — **let the land bring forth** — makes the ground the co-agent of animal life exactly as *tadshe ha-aretz* did for vegetation (v11). The two productive days frame the living world as brought out of the earth itself, under command.

The land animals are *nefesh chayah* — **living beings** — the same phrase used of the water and air creatures at v20 (see the note there on *nefesh* as breath/throat/life rather than a detachable soul), and *lemino*, **according to their kind**, is repeated across the three categories (cattle, creeping things, land-beasts). The verse withholds the verb *bara*: the animals are produced by the land, and only humankind, three verses later, will be *shaped* (*bara*, v. 27). The vocabulary marks the human as a distinct categorical act set against the continuum of earth-brought life.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ אֱלֹהִים֩ אֶת־חַיַּ֨ת הָאָ֜רֶץ לְמִינָ֗הּ וְאֶת־הַבְּהֵמָה֙ לְמִינָ֔הּ וְאֵ֛ת כָּל־רֶ֥מֶשׂ הָֽאֲדָמָ֖ה לְמִינֵ֑הוּ וַיַּ֥רְא אֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי־טֽוֹב׃

i18n.en: And the Elohim made the beasts of the land according to their kind, and the cattle according to their kind, and every creeping thing of the ground according to its kind. And the Elohim saw that it was good.
i18n.he: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ אֱלֹהִים֩ אֶת־חַיַּ֨ת הָאָ֜רֶץ לְמִינָ֗הּ וְאֶת־הַבְּהֵמָה֙ לְמִינָ֔הּ וְאֵ֛ת כָּל־רֶ֥מֶשׂ הָֽאֲדָמָ֖ה לְמִינֵ֑הוּ וַיַּ֥רְא אֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי־טֽוֹב׃
i18n.de: Und die Elohim machten die Tiere des Landes nach ihrer Art und das Vieh nach seiner Art und jedes kriechende Getier des Bodens nach seiner Art. Und die Elohim sahen, dass es gut war.
i18n.es: Y los Elohim hicieron las bestias de la tierra según su especie, y el ganado según su especie, y todo lo que se arrastra sobre el suelo según su especie. Y los Elohim vieron que era bueno.
i18n.fr: Et les Elohim firent les animaux de la terre selon leur espèce, et le bétail selon son espèce, et toute bête rampante du sol selon son espèce. Et les Elohim virent que cela était bon.
i18n.ja: エロヒムは地の獣をその種類にしたがって、家畜をその種類にしたがって、また土を這うすべてのものをその種類にしたがって造った。エロヒムはこれを見て、良しとした。
i18n.ko: 엘로힘은 그 종류대로 땅의 짐승을 만들었고, 그 종류대로 가축과, 그 종류대로 땅 위를 기는 모든 것을 만들었다. 엘로힘이 보니 좋았다.
i18n.ru: И сделали Элохим зверей земных по их роду, и скот по его роду, и всякое пресмыкающееся земли по его роду. И увидели Элохим, что это хорошо.
i18n.zh: 厄罗音按其类造了大地的走兽，按其类造了牲畜，又按其类造了一切在地上爬行之物。厄罗音看见这是好的。
i18n.zh-Hant: 厄羅音按其種類造了大地的走獸，按其種類造了牲畜，又按其種類造了一切爬行於地面之物。厄羅音看見這是好的。

notes.official: **Verb pattern note.** Land animals are *made* (*asah*), not *shaped* (*bara*). The chapter has now used *bara* twice (v1, v21) and *asah* many times. The third and final cluster of *bara* arrives in v27 for humankind.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֔ים נַֽעֲשֶׂ֥ה אָדָ֛ם בְּצַלְמֵ֖נוּ כִּדְמוּתֵ֑נוּ וְיִרְדּוּ֩ בִדְגַ֨ת הַיָּ֜ם וּבְע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֗יִם וּבַבְּהֵמָה֙ וּבְכָל־הָאָ֔רֶץ וּבְכָל־הָרֶ֖מֶשׂ הָֽרֹמֵ֥שׂ עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: And the Elohim said, "Let us make humankind in our image, according to our likeness; and let them rule over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the skies, and over the cattle, and over all the land, and over every creeping thing that creeps upon the land."
i18n.he: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֔ים נַֽעֲשֶׂ֥ה אָדָ֛ם בְּצַלְמֵ֖נוּ כִּדְמוּתֵ֑נוּ וְיִרְדּוּ֩ בִדְגַ֨ת הַיָּ֜ם וּבְע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֗יִם וּבַבְּהֵמָה֙ וּבְכָל־הָאָ֔רֶץ וּבְכָל־הָרֶ֖מֶשׂ הָֽרֹמֵ֥שׂ עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
i18n.de: Und die Elohim sagten: "Lasst uns Menschen machen in unserem Bild, nach unserem Ebenbild; und sie sollen herrschen über die Fische des Meeres und über die Vögel der Himmel und über das Vieh und über das ganze Land und über jedes kriechende Getier, das auf dem Land kriecht."
i18n.es: Y los Elohim dijeron: «Hagamos al ser humano a nuestra imagen, según nuestra semejanza; y que ellos gobiernen sobre los peces del mar, y sobre las aves de los cielos, y sobre el ganado, y sobre toda la tierra, y sobre toda cosa que se arrastra sobre la tierra».
i18n.fr: Et les Elohim dirent : « Faisons l'humanité à notre image, selon notre ressemblance ; et qu'ils dominent sur les poissons de la mer, et sur les oiseaux des cieux, et sur le bétail, et sur toute la terre, et sur toute bête rampante qui rampe sur la terre. »
i18n.ja: エロヒムは言った、「われわれの形にかたどり、われわれに似せて人を造ろう。そして彼らに、海の魚、天の鳥、家畜、地のすべて、また地の上を這うすべての這うものを治めさせよう」。
i18n.ko: 엘로힘이 말하였다, "우리 형상대로, 우리 모습을 따라 사람을 만들자; 그들이 바다의 물고기와, 하늘의 새와, 가축과, 온 땅과, 땅 위를 기는 모든 것을 다스리게 하자."
i18n.ru: И сказали Элохим: «Создадим человека по нашему образу, по нашему подобию; и да владычествуют они над рыбами морскими, и над птицами небесными, и над скотом, и над всею землёю, и над всяким пресмыкающимся, движущимся по земле».
i18n.zh: 厄罗音说：「让我们按我们的形象，依我们的样式造人；让他们管理海中的鱼、诸天的飞鸟、牲畜、整片大地，以及在大地上爬行的一切爬行之物。」
i18n.zh-Hant: 厄羅音說：「讓我們按我們的形象，依我們的樣式造人；讓他們管轄海中的魚、諸天的鳥、牲畜，以及全地，並一切爬行於大地之上的爬行物。」

notes.official:
**The central textual datum of the chapter, and the most-cited verse of the chapter for the WoH lens.** *Na'aseh* is the cohortative first-person **plural** of *asah* — *let us make*. It is grammatically unambiguous in Hebrew. The pronouns and possessives that follow are also plural: *b'tsalmenu* ("in **our** image"), *ki-dmutenu* ("according to **our** likeness").

Standard theological glosses include:

1. **Plural of majesty** — the royal "we". Ad hoc and not well-attested elsewhere in Hebrew for divine speech; the strongest objection is that *Elohim* never elsewhere governs first-person plural verbs of self-deliberation. Several Jewish commentators (Ibn Ezra, others) have endorsed this read but the textual support is weak.
2. **Trinitarian pre-figuring** — Christian retrojection; not a Hebrew-internal reading.
3. **Divine-council** — the modern scholarly consensus. the Elohim deliberates with attendant divine beings (cf. Job 1:6, Ps 82, 1 Kgs 22:19–22). The council reading reads the plural at face value but diffuses the agency.
4. **Literal plural agency** — the WoH lens reading. the Elohim deliberate as a plural agent in their own right.

The translation does **not** adjudicate. It preserves the grammar. The lens reading is one of the two textually defensible readings (alongside divine-council), and is the one the rest of the WoH corpus operates on.

*Adam* → **humankind**, not "man". *Ha-adam* is a category here, not a personal name (the named individual Adam appears later, in Gen 2–5). Gendered "man" is corrected (NJPS, NRSV both render "humankind"). The naming wordplay with *adamah* ("ground") will surface in Gen 2.

*On* tselem *itself.* Beyond its plurality, the noun *tselem* (צֶלֶם) carries a **concrete** sense that the conventional "image" obscures. In standard usage it denotes a carved or moulded figure — a statue, an idol, a cut-out physical likeness (the same word names the images at 2 Kgs 11:18, Amos 5:26, Dan 3:1); the Brown-Driver-Briggs gloss is "something cut out". Read against the ancient Near Eastern royal ideology, in which a king is set up as the living statue-image of his god, *b'tselem Elohim* describes the human as a material likeness of its makers rather than an abstract spiritual resemblance; the preposition *b'-* ("in / with / by means of") even permits *made with* the makers' likeness-bearing stuff, not only *in* their image. The translation keeps **"image"** — the concrete sense is available to the English reader — while narrowing the word to no single referent.

A further, **speculative** reading within the WoH lens takes that likeness-bearing material to be the carrier of biological information — genetic material, DNA — through which a likeness is physically transmitted. This extension goes well past what the lexicon settles: *tselem* supports "a concrete thing that carries a likeness", not any particular biochemistry. It is recorded here as an interpretive possibility, explicitly flagged as speculative; the translation asserts none of it.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּבְרָ֨א אֱלֹהִ֤ים ׀ אֶת־הָֽאָדָם֙ בְּצַלְמ֔וֹ בְּצֶ֥לֶם אֱלֹהִ֖ים בָּרָ֣א אֹת֑וֹ זָכָ֥ר וּנְקֵבָ֖ה בָּרָ֥א אֹתָֽם׃

i18n.en: And the Elohim shaped humankind in their image; in the image of the Elohim they shaped him; male and female they shaped them.
i18n.he: וַיִּבְרָ֨א אֱלֹהִ֤ים ׀ אֶת־הָֽאָדָם֙ בְּצַלְמ֔וֹ בְּצֶ֥לֶם אֱלֹהִ֖ים בָּרָ֣א אֹת֑וֹ זָכָ֥ר וּנְקֵבָ֖ה בָּרָ֥א אֹתָֽם׃
i18n.de: Und die Elohim formten die Menschen in ihrem Bild; im Bild der Elohim formten sie ihn; männlich und weiblich formten sie sie.
i18n.es: Y los Elohim formaron al ser humano a su imagen; a imagen de los Elohim lo formaron; varón y mujer los formaron.
i18n.fr: Et les Elohim façonnèrent l'humanité à leur image ; à l'image des Elohim ils le façonnèrent ; mâle et femelle ils les façonnèrent.
i18n.ja: エロヒムは人を彼らの形に形づくった。エロヒムの形に彼を形づくり、男と女とに彼らを形づくった。
i18n.ko: 엘로힘은 자신의 형상대로 사람을 빚었다; 엘로힘의 형상대로 그를 빚었다; 남자와 여자로 그들을 빚었다.
i18n.ru: И придали форму Элохим человеку по их образу; по образу Элохим они придали ему форму; мужчиной и женщиной они придали им форму.
i18n.zh: 厄罗音按他们的形象塑造了人；按厄罗音的形象塑造了他；有男有女，他们塑造了他们。
i18n.zh-Hant: 厄羅音按他們的形象塑造了人；按厄羅音的形象塑造了他；造了他們，有男有女。

notes.official:
**The verb pattern peaks: *bara* three times in one verse.** Humankind is *shaped* (*bara*), not just *made* (*asah*). The triple *bara* — once for the act, once for the image-specification, once for the male-and-female dimorphism — bookends the verb pattern of the chapter: v1 (skies and land), v21 (sea-creatures), v27 (humankind ×3). Categorical creation moments only.

**The plural-singular shift v26 → v27.** v26 has plural "Let us make … in **our** image" (*na'aseh … b'tsalmenu*), v27 has singular "in **his** image" (*b'tsalmo*) and singular subject *bara* ×3. The shift is textually real and the lens must address it. The natural reading: deliberative project speech (plural) → executing agency assignment (singular) within the Elohim group. The text supports a divine-council reading equally well; neither is forced.

*Tselem* and *demut* — **image** and **likeness**. The lexical core in Hebrew is **physical** resemblance:

- *Tselem* elsewhere denotes physical statues/representations: Num 33:52 (cast metal images), 1 Sam 6:5 (golden tumours/mice), Ezek 7:20, 16:17 (idol-statues).
- *Demut* elsewhere denotes bodily likeness: Ezek 1:5,10 ("the likeness as the appearance of a man"), 2 Kgs 16:10 (the pattern of an altar), 2 Chron 4:3.

Traditional Jewish and Christian readings spiritualize: humankind bears the Elohim's *moral* or *spiritual* image. The Hebrew lexicon supports physical resemblance **directly**, without interpretive extension. The lens reading is that the lexical core is the load-bearing data; the spiritualizing readings are extensions that may or may not be doing additional work.

paragraphs.text: וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֹתָם֮ אֱלֹהִים֒ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לָהֶ֜ם אֱלֹהִ֗ים פְּר֥וּ וּרְב֛וּ וּמִלְא֥וּ אֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ וְכִבְשֻׁ֑הָ וּרְד֞וּ בִּדְגַ֤ת הַיָּם֙ וּבְע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וּבְכָל־חַיָּ֖ה הָֽרֹמֶ֥שֶׂת עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: And the Elohim blessed them. And the Elohim said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the land, and subdue it; and rule over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the skies, and over every living thing that moves upon the land."
i18n.he: וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֹתָם֮ אֱלֹהִים֒ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לָהֶ֜ם אֱלֹהִ֗ים פְּר֥וּ וּרְב֛וּ וּמִלְא֥וּ אֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ וְכִבְשֻׁ֑הָ וּרְד֞וּ בִּדְגַ֤ת הַיָּם֙ וּבְע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וּבְכָל־חַיָּ֖ה הָֽרֹמֶ֥שֶׂת עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
i18n.de: Und die Elohim segneten sie. Und die Elohim sagten zu ihnen: "Seid fruchtbar und mehret euch und füllt das Land und unterwerft es; und herrscht über die Fische des Meeres und über die Vögel der Himmel und über jedes lebende Wesen, das sich auf dem Land regt."
i18n.es: Y los Elohim los bendijeron. Y los Elohim les dijeron: «Sed fecundos y multiplicaos, y llenad la tierra, y sométanla; y gobiernen sobre los peces del mar, y sobre las aves de los cielos, y sobre todo ser viviente que se mueve sobre la tierra».
i18n.fr: Et les Elohim les bénirent. Et les Elohim leur dirent : « Soyez féconds et multipliez-vous, et remplissez la terre, et soumettez-la ; et dominez sur les poissons de la mer, et sur les oiseaux des cieux, et sur tout être vivant qui se meut sur la terre. »
i18n.ja: エロヒムは彼らを祝福した。そしてエロヒムは彼らに言った、「産めよ、増えよ、地を満たし、これを従わせよ。また海の魚、天の鳥、地の上を動くすべての生き物を治めよ」。
i18n.ko: 엘로힘은 그들에게 복을 주었다. 그리고 엘로힘이 그들에게 말하였다, "생육하고 번성하여 땅을 채우라, 그리고 그것을 정복하고 다스리라; 바다의 물고기와 하늘의 새와 땅 위를 움직이는 모든 살아있는 것을 다스리라."
i18n.ru: И благословили их Элохим. И сказали им Элохим: «Плодитесь и размножайтесь, и наполняйте землю, и подчиняйте её; и владычествуйте над рыбами морскими, и над птицами небесными, и над всяким живым существом, движущимся по земле».
i18n.zh: 厄罗音赐福给他们。厄罗音对他们说：「要多产并繁衍，充满大地，征服并管理大地；管理海中的鱼、诸天的飞鸟，以及在大地上爬行的一切活物。」
i18n.zh-Hant: 厄羅音祝福他們。厄羅音對他們說：「要繁衍增多，充滿大地，征服並管理它；要管轄海中的魚、諸天的鳥，以及一切爬行於大地之上的活物。」

notes.official: *Kivshuha* ("subdue it") and *redu* ("rule") are strong verbs and not softened. *Kavash* in the Qal is forceful — "conquer", "bring under". *Radah* in the Qal denotes dominant rule, occasionally with the spatial sense of treading. Both verbs have been the subject of intense exegetical debate in environmental ethics since Lynn White Jr.'s 1967 thesis ("The Historical Roots of Our Ecologic Crisis"). The WoH translation does not paper over the strength; the interpretive question is a lens question, not a translation one.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים הִנֵּה֩ נָתַ֨תִּי לָכֶ֜ם אֶת־כָּל־עֵ֣שֶׂב ׀ זֹרֵ֣עַ זֶ֗רַע אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י כָל־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְאֶת־כָּל־הָעֵ֛ץ אֲשֶׁר־בּ֥וֹ פְרִי־עֵ֖ץ זֹרֵ֣עַ זָ֑רַע לָכֶ֥ם יִֽהְיֶ֖ה לְאָכְלָֽה׃

i18n.en: And the Elohim said, "Behold, I have given you every seed-bearing plant upon the face of all the land, and every tree in which is the fruit of a tree bearing seed; to you it shall be for food.
i18n.he: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים הִנֵּה֩ נָתַ֨תִּי לָכֶ֜ם אֶת־כָּל־עֵ֣שֶׂב ׀ זֹרֵ֣עַ זֶ֗רַע אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י כָל־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְאֶת־כָּל־הָעֵ֛ץ אֲשֶׁר־בּ֥וֹ פְרִי־עֵ֖ץ זֹרֵ֣עַ זָ֑רַע לָכֶ֥ם יִֽהְיֶ֖ה לְאָכְלָֽה׃
i18n.de: Und die Elohim sagten: "Siehe, ich habe euch jede samentragende Pflanze auf dem Angesicht des ganzen Landes gegeben und jeden Baum, an dem die Frucht eines samentragenden Baumes ist; euch soll es zur Nahrung sein.

notes.official:
**The original diet is exclusively plant-based — a point the priestly writer states with care.** *Le-okhlah* — **for food** — governs the grant: to humankind, *every seed-bearing plant* and *every tree with seed-bearing fruit*; to every animal, bird, and creeping thing (v30), *every green plant*. Nothing living is given as food to anything else. The primeval order the chapter describes is herbivorous and, by implication, non-predatory, for humans and beasts alike.

This is not incidental. Permission to eat meat is granted only after the flood, to Noah — *every moving thing that lives shall be food for you* (Gen 9:3) — worded there as an explicit extension of the plant grant of Eden, and hedged with the prohibition on blood. Commentators read Gen 1:29–30 and 9:3 as a deliberate pair: an original, bloodless creation order and its post-flood revision (so Sarna, and the broader analysis of the priestly diet ideology). The vegetarian ideal of the first creation is part of what makes the whole "very good" (v31), before the disruptions the later narratives record.

For the Wheel of Heaven reading, the pre-flood herbivorous order belongs with the other marks of a designed, non-violent original state — a baseline the subsequent history departs from, rather than an arbitrary rule. The claim the text itself asserts is narrow and direct: in the beginning, the food of every creature was green.

notes.official: **The grant extended to every animal.** The food-grant of v29 is widened to all land animals, birds, and creeping things — *yereq esev*, **every green plant**, a humbler category than the seed-plants and fruit assigned to humankind. The distinction is real: humankind receives the seed-bearing plants and fruit trees, the animals the green herbage; but both diets are wholly vegetal. *And it was so* closes the creative speech of day six before the summary verdict of v31.

notes.official: **The chapter closes.** *Yom ha-shishi* — **the sixth day**, with the definite article *ha-*. Days 2–5 lack the article; day 6 has it. The ordinal pattern with definite-article-on-day-6 marks day 6 as the culminating day, parallel to day one being marked by the cardinal *echad*. The numbered-day structure is deliberate and bookended. The closing *tov me'od* ("very good") intensifies the recurring formulaic "good" — six days of *tov*, peaking on day 6 with *tov me'od*.
